chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi', from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: My intercession on the Day of Judgment will not be granted to one who delays the obligatory prayer beyond its appointed time.

key_terms.الصلاة المفروضة: The obligatory prayer (salat al-mafrudha) — the five daily prayers mandated by God
key_terms.شفاعة: Intercession (shafa'a) — the Prophet's ability to intercede on behalf of believers before God on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.وقت: Appointed/prescribed time — each of the five prayers has a defined window

ai.seo_question: What happens if you delay your obligatory prayers beyond their time in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), as transmitted by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) through a chain of narrators, warns that those who habitually delay the obligatory daily prayers beyond their prescribed times will be deprived of his intercession on the Day of Judgment. This hadith stresses the critical importance of observing salat at its proper time and indicates that neglecting this duty — even without abandoning prayer entirely — has severe eschatological consequences. The audience of early Shia Muslims understood this as a strong exhortation to guard prayer times strictly.
